title: Choose the rebuilt Canvas structure
question: All three keep the Open Workbench identity, the three sample apps, and two honest entry paths. Which composition should carry the demo?

options.label: Workbench at first sight
options.thesis: The first viewport is already the product: choose a path, run a task, and watch the handoff happen beside the app.
options.viewport: A compact product header sits above a wide live workbench: scenario rail at left, the selected app in the center, and an honest Try demo / Connect your agent control rail at right; the activity trace begins within the same viewport.
options.risk: The integration story must stay legible without crowding the real app surface.

options.label: The proof corridor
options.thesis: A visitor advances through one visible chain from request to agent to browser action, with the selected app changing at each proof point.
options.viewport: A concise promise and two entry actions lead directly into a horizontal request-to-result path, while a large application viewport below shows the exact object the simulated or real agent changes.
options.risk: A staged sequence can feel scripted unless simulation labels and live event states are unmistakable.

options.label: The guided runbook
options.thesis: The page teaches the complete product loop as a short guided run whose steps remain real controls, not a slideshow.
options.viewport: A two-path start occupies the left half and a numbered four-step run occupies the right; choosing Try demo opens the first scenario in place, while Connect your agent reveals the HTTPS address field and OAuth explanation.
options.risk: Guidance can slow repeat visitors unless completed steps collapse cleanly.
